name: Kentucky

windshield.strip: transparent strip at the top not encroaching on the AS/1 area; OR (since July 15, 2024) material over the windshield with at least 70% light transmittance, not red or yellow

frontSide.note: film tested on 1/8-in. clear glass; reflectance max 25%

backSide.note: film tested on 1/8-in. clear glass; reflectance max 35%; perforated material min 30%

rear.note: same as windows behind driver; nontransparent rear window requires side mirrors on both sides

backSide.note: multipurpose passenger vehicles: film min 8% (tested on 1/8-in. clear glass), reflectance max 35%

rear.note: multipurpose passenger vehicles; side mirrors both sides if nontransparent

tint.measuredHow: film alone (tested on one-eighth inch clear glass); perforated material tested with existing glazing
tint.dualMirrors: Rear window nontransparent only if side mirrors on both sides (KRS 189.110(5))
tint.certificateOrSticker: Installer must affix a nonremovable compliance label to the inside left door jamb, with trade name and installer/seller business name (KRS 189.110(6))

medicalExemption.text: No medical exemption found in KRS 189.110.

penalty.text: Driver: fine $20-$100 per offense (KRS 189.990(1)(a)). Installer applying non-compliant film: Class B misdemeanor (KRS 189.110(9)).

quotes: if it has a light transmittance of not less than seventy percent (70%) and is not red or yellow in color.
a total solar reflectance of visible light of not more than twenty-five percent (25%) as measured on the nonfilm side and a light transmittance of at least thirty-five percent (35%)
not more than thirty-five percent (35%) as measured on the nonfilm side and a light transmittance of at least eighteen percent (18%) in the visible light range
a light transmittance of at least eight percent (8%) in the visible light range may be used on multipurpose passenger vehicles
Every percentage measurement required by subsections (2) to (4) of this section is subject to a tolerance of plus or minus three percent (3%).
shall be fined not less than twenty dollars ($20) nor more than one hundred dollars ($100) for each offense.

helmet.conditions: Under 21, instruction permit holders, and operators licensed less than one year

handheldPhone.noviceOrAgeBan: Drivers under 18 with permit, intermediate or operator's license may not use a personal communication device at all while moving (KRS 189.294)

studdedTires.cite: KRS 189.190 (regulates chains and lugs only; no stud restriction found)

radarDetector.note: No state ban on radar detectors in private passenger vehicles found; commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)

underglow.rule: Visible front lights only white or amber, visible rear lights only white, amber or red, unless original equipment; headlamps white only, no colored covers/film; solid blue lights treated as emergency-light violation

openQuestions: Studded tires: no Kentucky statute expressly allowing or restricting studs found; 'yes' is inferred from absence of a prohibition.
Primary enforcement of texting ban assumed (no secondary clause in KRS 189.292).
Lift/frame height: no Kentucky statute located.
